controller.scope: receiver delivery rate is not unused link capacity; healthy reports permit probes; source load includes framing, IDRs and admission-rejected units; all clocks and fixed-delay feedback are virtual

source_pilot.note: source provenance only; its historical frame-slot link differs from every byte-bounded replay

quality_comparison.note: same encoded source in all SIX arms; matched RGB quality excludes missing frames and uses only source IDs decoded by all six arms

sender.dispatch_window_note: half-open dispatch-time windows, including all bytes at each timestamp; endpoint ties within 1e-9 ms are excluded

service.formula: base = initial_target_kbps + 30 * 8 * fps / 1000; work_bits = debt_bits + 8 * pending_datagram_wire_bytes; queue service = min(base * max_rate_factor, max(base, work_bits / drain_ms)); fixed service = base; unpaced service = 0

sender.note: all attempted datagram wire bytes incur pacing debt regardless of downstream admission; local drops affect only unsent fragments and cannot refund debt; the frozen source receives no repair or encoder requests; service refreshes only after complete enqueue, expiry-chain removal and pop-plus-charge; original capture age is retained and idle credit is never accumulated

link.jitter_coupling: one seeded jitter draw per source sequence, precomputed independently of admission and shared by every fragment in that frame
link.loss_coupling: first-fragment erasure by source sequence; random loss keyed by seed, source sequence and fragment index, independently of admission
link.note: one atomic admission and serialization per group, charged the sum of exact datagram bytes; admitted bytes remain in flight until arrival including erasures; legacy frame-slot and frame-age settings are inactive; the receiver applies age

receiver.payload_note: datagram body bytes include the original CCV1 access-unit header; wire bytes additionally include the custom CCP1 datagram header
receiver.buffer_note: byte budget and peak count stored datagram bodies; frame metadata, temporary reconstruction and returned units are outside that byte count

batch_immediate.accounting_note: generated = local discard + attempted; attempted = admission rejected + admitted; admitted = erased + received; received = reassembled + unusable received. Reassembled frames may still be undecodable or late for presentation.

scope.clock: real local H.264; virtual source, packet dispatch, serialization, arrival and playout
scope.source: all replays freeze every pilot byte, timestamp and encoder action; no new feedback or repair
scope.headers: all arms charge identical CCP1 custom datagrams including every 16-byte fragment header
scope.service: configured independent allowance retains initial target plus nominal 30-byte AU framing; fragment headers are fully charged but do not increase that inherited base; not known capacity
scope.rejection: sender schedule is computed without admission or erasure input; rejected fragments do not abort later attempts for the same frame
scope.granularity: batch arms admit and serialize all frame datagrams atomically; packet arms do so individually
scope.attribution: batch_fixed versus packet_fixed isolates granularity under fixed service; batch_service versus packet_service also changes service refresh cadence
scope.receiver: only complete validated exact access units enter H.264; no partial decode or concealment; never-observed frames are evaluator-known missing, not receiver-detected timeouts
scope.bounds: local bounds count frames with unsent data; receiver byte bound counts stored fragment bodies; source clocks and full presentation horizon are preserved
scope.limits: bounded synthetic frozen-source experiment; no RTP/FU-A interoperability, UDP/IP accounting, retransmission, FEC, physical network/display, Colab allocation or transport feedback controller
